jesse: Quick sync — Starlit POC (private) needs creds for a Private deployment. They require HSM-backed root keys and short-lived client certs issued via our cert-broker. Who's owning the handoff?
rachel: I can lead presales on this. Need a checklist of artifacts we expect from the customer and the exchange method (PKCS#11, SCEP, or manual CSR).
mina: Security note: prefer PKCS#11 + attestation where possible. If customer can't do PKCS#11 we can accept SCEP with OIDC client auth, otherwise manual CSR for initial bootstrap only. Also we require CA chain and attestation cert.
aditya: For Dedicated pool sizing: Starlit said they want ~150 qps and 1k concurrent users for inference. That maps to ~4x A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline, i'll validate. Pricing we quoted previously should be adjustable for a 30d trial.
jesse: Can you list exact items we need them to upload to the secure share? I'll send a clear checklist to the customer. :+1:
rachel: Checklist draft: 1) CA cert chain (PEM) 2) If PKCS#11: module path + token label + slot + attestation cert 3) If SCEP: enrollment URL + OIDC client creds 4) CSR (if manual) 5) Allowed CIDR/IPs for management plane 6) Bastion SSH pubkey and jump host details 7) Contact + SLAs for cert rotation
mina: Add: HSM manufacturer & firmware version (for FIPS/CCL checks), and key usage/policy (non-exportable, sign/decrypt flags). We also need a timeline for rotation windows and whether they allow our ephemeral CA cert signing.
aditya: Also ask whether they want model pinning to the Dedicated pool or route traffic to hosted fallback on overload. That impacts capacity planning and the fallback pricing tier.
jesse: Good — also they asked about the cert exchange transport. Propose we support three paths: 1) PKCS#11 over VPN (preferred) 2) SCEP + OIDC 3) Manual CSR via secure upload. Which should we push?
mina: Push PKCS#11 over a customer-hosted VPN/bastion for production. For POC we can accept SCEP or manual CSR but mark as limited (no attestation). Include steps for PKCS#11 attestation:
```
# example CSR generation from HSM PKCS#11
# (customer runs this and shares CSR)
pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so -l --pin PIN --keypairgen --key-type rsa:2048 -o private.key
openssl req -engine pkcs11 -keyform engine -new -key "pkcs11:object=customer_key;type=private" -out starlit.csr -subj "/CN=starlit-client/O=Starlit"
```
mina: And what we will provide back (after verification): short-lived client cert (24h-7d), cert revocation endpoint, and a signed attestation token for the pool.
rachel: For the secure transfer we will create a temporary S3 share with MFA delete and pre-signed PUTs, or set up an SFTP user scoped to the upload path. Which does Starlit prefer?
jesse: I'll ask them; likely S3 presigned. Also they want audit logs forwarded to their SIEM — add that to the checklist.
aditya: Quick note on pricing: if they pin models to Dedicated we include reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit). For a 30d POC we can offer a reduced commit and trial credits against overage. I'll draft a number after I confirm GPU type.
devops-bot: :package: Ticket INF-4827 created: "starlit private-poc cert exchange + hsm attestation" — assignee: rachel, eta: 3 business days. Link: https://rwd.atlassian/INF-4827
mina: Security follow-ups I'll need from Starlit: signed ATO doc for POC, SOC2 evidence (if available), and the PKCS#11 test vector to validate signing operations.
jesse: Timeline ask to customer: please provide artifacts within 5 business days to hit our 2-week POC window. I'll CC solutions and security in the kickoff.
rachel: I'll prepare the handoff email and include the checklist + sample commands above. Will ping once INF-4827 has a PRD attachment.
jesse: Great — thanks team. I'll message Starlit now and update thread with their chosen transfer method. :rocket:
